subject.title: [Feature]: Import Codex and Claude Code memory from Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-class Control UI import for private Codex and Claude durable memory, and if so, what local-host versus remote-Gateway trust boundary must it enforce?
rationale: The provider architecture can support memory items, but exposing private filesystem discovery and persistent copying through Gateway and Control UI is a product and security policy choice that automation cannot safely resolve.

options.title: Sponsor secure full flow
options.body: Approve provider-owned allowlisted discovery plus metadata-only preview, explicit selection, backups, conflict handling, cancellation, and redacted reporting across Gateway and Control UI.

options.title: Implement CLI items first
options.body: Add memory items to the existing CLI migration providers and defer Control UI exposure until remote-Gateway authorization and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Retain manual import
options.body: Keep durable memory outside automated migration and document a safe selective-copy procedure instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor secure full flow
recommendation.body: Approve provider-owned allowlisted discovery plus metadata-only preview, explicit selection, backups, conflict handling, cancellation, and redacted reporting across Gateway and Control UI.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the concrete cross-surface product contract and is the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether OpenClaw should sponsor it.
